name: Coldveil Switchback Street Operative Set
description: A reversible field jacket anchors this set — one side is a muted oxblood-brown textured ripstop with scanner-diffusing nano-weave panels across the shoulders and chest, the other a deep slate grey with subtle hex-pattern embossing. The jacket hits mid-hip with a structured collar that folds up into a partial face shield, magnetic snap closures running down the left chest, and concealed holster channels sewn into both interior breast panels. The left sleeve has a chrome-routed aug-power channel running from cuff to shoulder with an external snap-open seam for arm prosthetic access. Worn open, it reads as a beat-up logistics worker's coat. Closed and reversed, it becomes something quieter and harder to place. Underneath is a dark burgundy moisture-wicking compression turtleneck with embedded comm-relay threading along the collar seam. The trousers are a charcoal-toned articulated ripstop with four concealed zippered thigh pockets, reinforced knee panels, and a gusseted crotch for full-range movement. Footwear is a low-profile matte black ankle boot with a rubber-compound sole engineered for silence on metal grating and wet concrete, with a magnetic closure hidden under a false lace panel. The overall silhouette reads Tier 2-3 — just another person moving through Circuit with something to carry.
functionality: Reversible jacket for rapid visual identity change; concealed dual holster channels; aug-power routing channel in left sleeve with snap-open access seam; scanner-diffusing shoulder and chest panels; comm-relay threading in collar; four concealed zippered thigh pockets; reinforced knees; partial face-shield collar fold; silent-sole footwear
what_it_says: This outfit says someone who has done this long enough to stop showing it. No excess, no posturing — just a person who knows exactly what they need and has sewn it into every seam. The reversible jacket is the tell for anyone who knows what to look for. Everyone else sees a slightly tired Tier 2 worker heading somewhere they don't need to explain.
worn_by: fixers who move between tiers regularly
story_hooks: A runner reverses the jacket mid-transit after a witness description goes out over the corpsec band — the jacket's scanner-diffusing panels have already scrambled the last checkpoint's biometric sweep, but they don't know yet if it worked.
The comm-relay threading in the collar collar has been broadcasting on a frequency the runner didn't authorize — someone has been listening to every job for the last three weeks.

A contact refuses to meet unless the runner shows up looking like Tier 2. The reversible jacket is the only thing standing between a successful handoff and a blown cover in a crowd of factory shift workers.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately ambiguous operative silhouette that shifts between industrial worker and tactical operative depending on which side of the reversible jacket faces outward. The oxblood-brown side reads as worn-in logistics wear; the slate grey side becomes more purposeful and covert. Mid-hip length maintains mobility while the structured collar and compression turtleneck create a contained, ready posture. Dark, muted palette throughout suggests someone moving through urban spaces without drawing attention.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not tight—structured through the shoulders with enough room for augmented limbs and concealed gear, compression fit through the torso from the turtleneck, articulated at the hips and thighs for crouched movement and rapid repositioning. The trousers have a subtle taper at the ankle but sit relaxed through the leg for unrestricted access to concealed pockets.
physical_description.primary_material: Reversible ripstop shell (oxblood-brown and slate grey), scanner-diffusing nano-weave panels, moisture-wicking compression fabric (turtleneck), matte-finish ballistic synthetic leather (boots), integrated copper-trace comm threading
physical_description.texture: Ripstop has a subtle woven roughness with nano-weave panels creating microscopic diffusion patterns; compression turtleneck is smooth and body-hugging; the hex-pattern embossing on the grey side is barely perceptible to touch but catches light at certain angles; boots feature a soft matte rubber compound designed to absorb impact noise
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: oxblood-brown and slate grey (reversible). Secondary: deep burgundy compression layer visible at collar and cuffs. Accents: chrome-routed power channel on left sleeve, matte black boots. No logos or bright trim—all detailing is functional or recessed.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap closures down the left chest of jacket (five snaps, low-profile profile); friction-fit gusseted seams on compression turtleneck; hidden magnetic closure on boots beneath false lace panel; zippered thigh pockets on trousers (four, low-profile sliders); snap-open seam along aug-power channel
distinctive_features: Reversible construction—oxblood ripstop vs. slate grey hex-embossed side
Integrated scanner-diffusing nano-weave panels across shoulders and chest
Structured collar that folds up into partial face shield configuration
Chrome-routed aug-power channel with external snap-open seam for prosthetic arm integration
Concealed holster channels in both interior breast panels
Embedded comm-relay threading along turtleneck collar seam
Four concealed zippered thigh pockets with reinforced panels
Silent-sole engineering on ankle boots for noise-dampening on metal grating
False lace panel concealing magnetic boot closure
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 crossover—expensive enough to contain functional augmentation integration and signal someone with access to black-market Circuit District gear, but deliberately unglamorous enough to avoid corporate surveillance attention or street predation
physical_description.cultural_context: Street operative, logistics cover identity, augmentation-adjacent (prosthetic or implant-ready). The reversibility suggests someone who needs to code-switch between working-class mundanity and tactical purpose. Worn by Circuit District fixers, independent couriers, and mid-tier grey-market operatives who can't afford to be memorable.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained—the oxblood side shows minor creasing and scuff patterns consistent with regular use; the grey side remains crisper, suggesting it's deployed less frequently or kept in rotation. Seams are sound, closures function smoothly, no visible rips or patches. The wear is intentional and curated, not accidental.
